SLOOS adjustment: The July 2022 SLOOS indicates banks tightened standards and terms for C&I loans (across firm sizes) and CRE, raised loan pricing and collateral requirements, and tightened in many residential categories (including subprime), while reporting stronger C&I and HELOC demand but weaker CRE demand. This survey evidence of tightening bank credit supply implies an additional drag on growth and financial conditions independent of Fed actions, modestly tempering the hawkish read from the FOMC’s “ongoing increases” guidance and accelerated QT. Net: still clearly hawkish due to the inflation focus and balance sheet runoff, but slightly less so once SLOOS tightening is incorporated.
